scenes.narration: Can a Prime Minister remove India's Chief Election Commissioner? Not alone. The Constitution gives the CEC the same protection as a Supreme Court judge.

scenes.narration: On 27 October, at a public hearing in Trilokpuri, Delhi, Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi said protests against the voter-list revision, called SIR, will continue until CEC Gyanesh Kumar resigns or the Prime Minister removes him.

scenes.speaker: Aditya

scenes.narration: On 7 October, according to Reuters and AFP, Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders were detained while marching to Jantar Mantar. They were released that evening.

scenes.speaker: Nisha

scenes.narration: Here is the rule. Under Article 324(5), a CEC can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian man, about 34, news anchor, medium-brown skin, short curly black hair, light stubble, rimless glasses, charcoal blazer over a black crew-neck, in a dark studio, explaining to camera with a steady expression, medium shot

scenes.narration: On proved misbehaviour or incapacity, by a motion passed in both Houses with a special majority, then an order of the President. The Election Commission made the same point in an affidavit to the Supreme Court.
scenes.on_screen_text: Both Houses, special majority, President's order

scenes.speaker: Aditya

scenes.narration: On 6 April 2026, according to All India Radio, Speaker Om Birla and Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan rejected an opposition notice for such a motion.

scenes.narration: According to Reuters, the Election Commission and the BJP deny the opposition's accusations. In its affidavit, the Commission says its SIR decisions followed the law.
